newsitem.title: USA: FDX still working on Paris-Subic route date.
newsitem.headline: FDX still working on Paris-Subic route date.

text.p: Federal Express Corp is still working on plans for the proposed service eastwards from its Paris hub to its Subic Bay hub in the Philippines, Fedex executive vice-president worldwide operations, Theodore Weise said.
He told journalists that the service would start "sooner than later" adding "it would be sometime in the next 24 months," but declined to give a more precise date.

In spring 1996, Fedex announced long-term plans to increase traffic at Paris-Charles de Gaulle through a global service routing Memphis-Paris-Dubai to Subic Bay. An agreement was also recently signed under which the Paris airport authority (ADP) and Fedex will each invest around 500 million francs in the hub's expansion.
One of the reasons for the delay in the launch date was assessing whether sufficient traffic already exists for the service, Weise added.

He also said that no decision has yet been taken as to which aircraft will be used: "A McDonnell-Douglas DC-10-30 freighter seems most likely to start with, but other possibilities include a MD-11 freighter or an Airbus Industrie A300 freighter.

At present European traffic for Asia is generally routed via Memphis and through the Anchorage hub to Subic Bay for intra-Asian distribution. In some cases it could be moved via other carriers eastwards to Asia for eventual collection and delivery by Fedex.
Separately Weise said Fedex's competitors :"have very difficult problems in front of them because of the need to get regulatory rights to fly to other countries."

The acquisition of Flying Tiger Inc's in 1989 with routes to 21 countries:"provided rights which were simply not (otherwise) available," he added, "and to duplicate our capability is going to be extraordinarily difficult."
"Fedex intends to exploit this advantage, " Weise said. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
